$comment: The deliberate-n/a register (#890 W6). tests/matrix.json carries 56 cells that are deliberately not owned, and validate-app-axes.mjs already checks their citations resolve. What nothing checked is the distinction that decides whether a cell is finished: an IMPOSSIBILITY (the claim cannot arise — the citation is the whole proof) and a PROHIBITION (the claim must never arise, so something must FAIL when it does) read identically in the matrix, which is exactly why the difference rotted invisibly. scripts/audit-na-cells.mjs holds this file against the matrix on every PR.
$no-backfill: #890's non-goals say plainly: do NOT backfill these cells. The ritual is re-verification, not conversion. A row's `reviewed` date is what makes it a ritual rather than a register — the audit fails a row nobody has re-read within two quarters, and the only way to clear that is to read the cell against its citation and re-date it. Bumping the date without reading the cell is the one move the audit cannot detect and the only one that makes it worthless.
$seeded: Seeded 2026-08-30 by #890, which IS this register's first review: every row was read against its matrix citation as it was written. Rows whose matrix `reason` was already a full re-verification carry it; the nine that were fragments ("Agenda is structurally record-only.") were restated at length, because a fragment cannot tell a later reader whether the ruling still applies.

appSeats.locker.viewer.restated: Locker declares `seats.disabledOn: ["viewer"]`, so this is not an absence of behaviour but a required one: the PWA seat must REFUSE at the mount path rather than render the app. Something has to fail if a browser ever mounts Locker, which is why this cell is a prohibition and names the gate that fails.

appSeats.tally.viewer.restated: Tally's v17 web interface shipped and its doors and drawn surface are covered at the unit and component tiers; what is absent is the seat's end-to-end journey, which is scheduled work rather than a claim that cannot be made. Re-read when #872's e2e follow-up lands — this is the one row here most likely to stop being an n/a.

appEngines.agenda.placement.restated: Agenda has no placeable entity in the shared registry.

appEngines.agenda.custody.restated: Agenda holds no bytes — every event is a row, and `seats.byteBearing` is false in its manifest. Custody is a claim about who holds a blob and can restore it; with no blob there is no such claim to make, and an owner would have to invent the situation it tested.

appEngines.agenda.consent.restated: Agenda is outside the closed enrichment-domain union.

appEngines.agenda.triage.restated: Triage is the proposal-queue engine: it exists for apps that receive candidate rows a member must accept or reject. Agenda's manifest declares no proposal queue, so there is no queue to drain and no proposal to adjudicate.

appEngines.agenda.search.restated: Agenda does not consume the shared search scaffold.

appEngines.docs.triage.restated: Docs has no shipped correction-proposal queue.

appEngines.docs.search.restated: Docs does not consume the shared search scaffold.

appEngines.locker.placement.restated: Locker is structurally excluded from placement.

appEngines.locker.consent.restated: Locker is outside the closed enrichment-domain union.

appEngines.locker.triage.restated: Locker declares no proposal queue, and deliberately: a secret arrives because the member put it there, never as a candidate something else proposed. There is nothing for triage to adjudicate.

appEngines.locker.search.restated: Locker does not consume the shared search scaffold.

appEngines.notes.consent.restated: Notes is outside the closed enrichment-domain union.

appEngines.notes.triage.restated: Notes declares no proposal queue. A note is authored, not proposed — the share-intent ingest path writes directly rather than queueing a candidate — so triage has no queue to drain.

appEngines.notes.search.restated: Notes does not consume the shared search scaffold.

appEngines.people.placement.restated: People has no placeable entity in the shared registry.

appEngines.people.custody.restated: People holds no bytes: a party is rows and channels, and `seats.byteBearing` is false. An avatar, when one exists, is a `core_attachment` owned by the content spine's custody, not by this app's.

appEngines.people.consent.restated: People is outside the closed enrichment-domain union.

appEngines.people.triage.restated: People declares no proposal queue. Contact writeback reconciles against existing parties through the shared dedupe module rather than queueing candidates for adjudication.

appEngines.people.search.restated: People does not consume the shared search scaffold.

appEngines.tally.custody.restated: Tally is record-only; its receipt-photo origin edge does not import custody.

appEngines.tally.consent.restated: Tally is outside the closed enrichment-domain union.

appEngines.tally.triage.restated: Tally declares no proposal queue. An expense is entered or materialised from a recurring template; neither shape produces a candidate row awaiting a member's yes.

appEngines.tasks.placement.restated: Tasks has no placeable entity in the shared registry.

appEngines.tasks.custody.restated: Tasks holds no bytes — a task is a row, and `seats.byteBearing` is false. Attachments on a task are `core_attachment` rows under the content spine's custody, not this app's.

appEngines.tasks.consent.restated: Tasks is outside the closed enrichment-domain union.

appEngines.tasks.triage.restated: Tasks declares no proposal queue. Tasks are authored or materialised from a recurrence; there is no inbound candidate stream for triage to adjudicate.

appEngines.tasks.search.restated: Tasks does not consume the shared search scaffold.

surface.vault-core.offline.restated: Skip: vault is a storage primitive; offline UX is exercised by mobile.offline + web.offline consuming surfaces.

surface.vault-core.journey.restated: Skip: no end-user vault journey surface; blank-machine restore owns backup-restore.journey and search/enrichment flows own vault correctness paths.

surface.blob-custody.offline.restated: Skip: blob store has no offline user journey; durability is ENOSPC custody + disk-full e2e; offline is a consuming-surface concern.

surface.blob-custody.compat.restated: Skip: no blob format migration path in v0; CBSF mutation + format floors cover format stability instead.

surface.blob-custody.journey.restated: Skip: custody is a primitive; journeys live on mobile upload durability and desktop/gateway blob consumers.

surface.backup-restore.concurrency.restated: Skip: restore into a LIVE gateway was deleted with the founding plane (#603) — restore is the offline `recover` verb, so concurrent restore has no surface.

surface.backup-restore.offline.restated: Skip: restore is an online blank-machine operation; offline continuity is owned by vault WAL + mobile offline, not backup kit.

surface.gateway.offline.restated: Skip: gateway is always the online host; offline UX lives on mobile/web clients. No meaningful gateway-offline matrix cell.

surface.gateway.compat.restated: Skip: no gateway wire migration suite in v0; protocol judge + tunnel wire contracts own compatibility pressure.

surface.app-engine.offline.restated: Skip: app-engine runs server-side with the gateway; offline is a client-surface dimension.

surface.app-engine.compat.restated: Skip: no app-engine API migration surface in v0; harness registry contracts own kind-compat pressure.

surface.app-engine.journey.restated: Skip: user journeys are desktop/web/mobile copilot paths; engine is exercised via agent-runtime.journey (fake-acp).

surface.automations.offline.restated: Skip: automations schedule on the gateway host; offline client behavior is mobile/web. No offline scheduler product path.

surface.automations.compat.restated: Skip: no automations schema migration in v0; scheduler mutation floors cover pure compute stability.

surface.agent-runtime.offline.restated: Skip: harnesses require a live CLI/ACP process; offline is not a runtime dimension (client offline owns UX).

surface.extension.durability.restated: Structural N/A: the extension owns no durable state; paired credentials are browser storage and gateway-owned.

surface.extension.concurrency.restated: Structural N/A for v0: one active popup/worker transaction is admitted per browser profile.

surface.extension.performance.restated: Structural N/A for v0: the companion performs no user-visible compute or transfer hot path.

surface.extension.scalability.restated: Structural N/A for v0: one companion serves one browser profile; fleet scale belongs to the gateway.

surface.extension.compat.restated: Structural N/A until a versioned extension storage format exists; gateway protocol contracts own wire compatibility.

surface.oauth-worker.durability.restated: Structural N/A: the OAuth courier intentionally holds no durable application state.

surface.oauth-worker.concurrency.restated: Structural N/A: stateless Cloudflare Worker isolates provide request concurrency; no shared mutable state exists.

surface.oauth-worker.performance.restated: Structural N/A: provider and edge latency dominate the stateless one-shot code courier.

surface.oauth-worker.scalability.restated: Structural N/A: Cloudflare owns isolate scaling and the courier holds no application queue or pool.

surface.oauth-worker.offline.restated: Structural N/A: an edge OAuth callback service has no offline product mode.

surface.oauth-worker.compat.restated: Structural N/A: the courier exposes one versionless, short-lived exchange contract owned by contract tests.

surface.oauth-worker.journey.restated: Structural N/A: end-user OAuth journeys are owned by the consuming desktop/web surfaces; the worker is a stateless courier.
